types.oie_definition: A numerical value or proportion representing a count, amount, or frequency.
types.embedding_query_text: Quantity/Statistic: A numerical value or proportion representing a count, amount, or frequency. Also called number, amount, proportion, figure.

chosen_type.label: NumericalStatistic
chosen_type.definition: A numerical value, count, or proportion representing a statistic or measurable amount.
chosen_type.justification: Existing Schema.org `Quantity` is too focused on measurable amounts with standard units, while `Number` is too generic. The mentions are specific numerical expressions of counts or proportions.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

types.oie_definition: A general classification or group of food items sharing common characteristics or uses.
types.embedding_query_text: Food Category: A general classification or group of food items sharing common characteristics or uses. Also called food group, food type, cuisine, dietary category.

chosen_type.label: FoodCategory
chosen_type.definition: A classification or group of food items sharing common characteristics or uses.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org class directly represents a general food category; existing candidates are too specific (e.g., menu sections) or irrelevant.

mentions: foods marketed to children between 6 and 36 months

candidates.label: FoodEvent
candidates.comment: A FoodEvent is an Event centered around food and drink. Also called culinary event, gastronomic event, food festival. Examples: A wine tasting, a cooking class, a food fair, a restaurant week promotion.

candidates.label: MenuSection
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a sub-grouping of food or drink items within a menu. Also called menu category, food section, course. Examples: "Appetizers", "Main Courses", "Desserts", "Drinks", "Vegan Options". Distinct from Menu, which is the entire list.

candidates.label: DrugClass
candidates.comment: A DrugClass is a MedicalEntity representing a category of medical drugs, grouped by general pharmacological class, common mechanisms of action, or physiological effects. Also called drug category, medication group, therapeutic class. Examples: Statins, Antibiotics, Antidepressants, Beta-blockers.

candidates.label: FoodService
candidates.comment: A FoodService is a Service related to providing food, such as breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Also called meal service, catering service, dining option. Examples: Breakfast service at a hotel, a school lunch program, an in-flight meal service, a catering package for an event.

candidates.label: MenuItem
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a single food or drink item listed within a menu or menu section. Also called menu item, dish, beverage. Examples: "Spaghetti Carbonara", "Caesar Salad", "Coca-Cola", "Chocolate Lava Cake". Distinct from Menu, which is the entire list.

types.oie_definition: A level of quality, achievement, or measure against which something is judged or compared.
types.embedding_query_text: Standard: A level of quality, achievement, or measure against which something is judged or compared. Also called benchmark, guideline, criterion, specification.

chosen_type.label: Standard
chosen_type.definition: A level of quality, achievement, or measure against which something is judged or compared.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org class directly represents a general standard; existing candidates are either too specific (e.g., medical, energy) or represent the act of certification rather than the standard itself.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

candidates.label: MedicalEvidenceLevel
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing the level of evidence supporting a medical guideline. Also called evidence strength, guideline reliability, data quality level. Examples: "Level A evidence", "Grade 1 recommendation", "strong evidence".

candidates.label: MedicalGuidelineContraindication
candidates.comment: A medical guideline that specifically designates a process as harmful, supported by sound data. Also called contraindicated guideline, harmful practice warning, medical prohibition. Examples: "guideline against routine antibiotic use for viral infections", "contraindication for specific surgical techniques". Distinct from MedicalGuidelineRecommendation, which suggests an efficacious process.

candidates.label: EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an Enumeration of energy efficiency levels and certifications from various international standards. Also called energy rating, efficiency class, energy certification. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration, EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration.

candidates.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
candidates.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

types.oie_definition: A Uniform Resource Locator, an address that specifies the location of a resource on the internet.
types.embedding_query_text: URL: A Uniform Resource Locator, an address that specifies the location of a resource on the internet. Also called web address, link, internet address.

chosen_type.label: URL
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `URL` datatype directly represents a Uniform Resource Locator, which perfectly matches the OIE type and mention.

candidates.label: URL
candidates.comment: A data type representing a Uniform Resource Locator, which specifies the address of a resource on the internet. Also called web address, link, internet address. Examples: "https://schema.org", "ftp://example.com/file.zip", "mailto:info@example.com".

candidates.label: BreadcrumbList
candidates.comment: A BreadcrumbList is an ItemList representing a hierarchical navigation path, typically on a website, showing the user's current location relative to the site's structure. Also called navigation path, breadcrumbs, site path. Examples: Home > Products > Electronics > Televisions, Blog > Category > Post Title.

candidates.label: WebPage
candidates.comment: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.

candidates.label: WPFooter
candidates.comment: The bottom section of a web page, typically containing copyright information, contact details, and navigation links. Also called page footer, website footer, site bottom. Examples: the copyright notice at the bottom of a website, links to privacy policy and terms of service, social media icons in the footer.

candidates.label: LinkRole
candidates.comment: A LinkRole is an intangible role representing a Web link, allowing for the specification of link relationships and other HTML link element details outside of HTML. Also called URL role, hyperlink descriptor, web link attribute. Examples: a link with 'linkRelationship' 'amphtml', a canonical URL link, a link to a related resource.

types.oie_definition: A specific day of the calendar year.
types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific day of the calendar year. Also called calendar date, day, specific day.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `Date` datatype directly represents a specific calendar date, which perfectly matches the OIE type and mention.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.oie_definition: A classification of individuals based on their age range or developmental stage.
types.embedding_query_text: Age Group: A classification of individuals based on their age range or developmental stage. Also called demographic group, life stage, age bracket.

chosen_type.label: SizeGroupEnumeration
chosen_type.justification: This enumeration includes 'Kids' as an example, which aligns with the mentions being classifications of individuals by age, even though the name implies physical size.

candidates.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
candidates.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

candidates.label: SizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups used for various product categories. Also called size category, apparel size group, product size range. Examples: 'Adult', 'Kids', 'Petite', 'Plus Size'.

candidates.label: WearableSizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups or types for wearable products. Also called apparel size group, clothing size type, garment category. Examples: "men's", "women's", "children's", "unisex".

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: GenderType
candidates.comment: A GenderType is an Enumeration of genders. Also called sex, gender identity. Examples: Male, Female, NonBinary.

types.oie_definition: A nation or state, typically with its own government and territory.
types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation or state, typically with its own government and territory. Also called nation, state, land.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `Country` class directly represents a sovereign state or nation, which perfectly matches the OIE type and mentions.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.oie_definition: A systematic investigation or experiment designed to discover or revise facts, theories, or applications.
types.embedding_query_text: Research Study: A systematic investigation or experiment designed to discover or revise facts, theories, or applications. Also called study, investigation, experiment, academic paper.

chosen_type.label: ResearchProject
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `ResearchProject` class directly represents a planned enterprise for scientific inquiry, explicitly listing "study" as an alias, which perfectly matches the OIE type and mentions.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: ScholarlyArticle
candidates.comment: A formal article presenting original research or analysis, typically peer-reviewed and published in an academic journal. Also called academic paper, research article, journal publication, scientific paper. Examples: a paper published in Nature, a research article in the Journal of Marketing, a thesis chapter.

candidates.label: MedicalTrial
candidates.comment: A medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or procedures, typically with random allocation to groups. Also called clinical trial, randomized controlled trial, interventional study. Examples: a Phase 3 drug trial, a study comparing two surgical techniques, a vaccine efficacy trial. Distinct from MedicalObservationalStudy, where treatment assignment is not controlled by the investigator.

types.oie_definition: A specific place or position.
types.embedding_query_text: Location: A specific place or position. Also called place, site, area, spot.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `Place` class is a general entity for locations with physical extension, which encompasses all the diverse mentions of specific places.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: Seat
candidates.comment: A specific seating location, often reserved, within an event venue or transportation. Also called reserved spot, seating assignment, chair, place. Examples: seat 12A on an airplane, row F seat 5 at a concert, a specific table at a restaurant.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

types.oie_definition: A structured group of people with a particular purpose, such as a company, institution, or association.
types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose, such as a company, institution, or association. Also called institution, association, agency, body.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `Organization` class directly represents a group of people with a particular purpose, which perfectly matches the OIE type and all mentions.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

types.oie_definition: A function or position that a person or entity has in a particular context or activity.
types.embedding_query_text: Role: A function or position that a person or entity has in a particular context or activity. Also called position, function, capacity, job.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `Role` class broadly describes a function or position, which perfectly encompasses all the diverse mentions of roles.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

types.oie_definition: A place where goods are sold directly to consumers.
types.embedding_query_text: Retail Outlet: A place where goods are sold directly to consumers. Also called store, shop, market, retailer.

chosen_type.label: Store
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `Store` class directly represents a retail business selling goods to consumers, which perfectly matches the OIE type and mentions.

candidates.label: OutletStore
candidates.comment: An OutletStore is a local business that sells goods, often at reduced prices, directly from a manufacturer or retailer. Also called factory outlet, discount store, clearance store. Examples: a Nike outlet, a designer brand outlet, a retail chain's clearance center. Distinct from DepartmentStore, which sells a wide range of goods at regular prices.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

candidates.label: WholesaleStore
candidates.comment: A local business that sells goods in large quantities, typically to retailers or other businesses, rather than directly to individual consumers. Also called wholesaler, bulk store, cash and carry. Examples: Costco Business Center, a restaurant supply store, a building materials wholesaler.

candidates.label: ConvenienceStore
candidates.comment: A local business retail store offering a limited range of everyday items, often with extended hours. Also called corner store, mini-mart, quick shop. Examples: 7-Eleven, Circle K, a local neighborhood market, a gas station store. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.

candidates.label: DepartmentStore
candidates.comment: A type of store that sells a wide variety of consumer goods across different departments. Also called Retail department store, general merchandise store. Examples: Macy's, Nordstrom, Harrods, Kohl's. Distinct from Store, which is a general category for any retail establishment.

types.oie_definition: An individual human being.
types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, figure.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `Person` class directly represents an individual human being, which perfectly matches the OIE type and mentions.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: ProfilePage
candidates.comment: A ProfilePage is a WebPage dedicated to displaying information about a specific entity, such as a person or organization. Also called user profile, personal page, bio page. Examples: a LinkedIn profile, a social media user's page, an author's biography page, a company's "About Us" page.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

types.oie_definition: A job or profession, especially one requiring special training, followed as one's main career.
types.embedding_query_text: Occupation: A job or profession, especially one requiring special training, followed as one's main career. Also called job title, profession, vocation, career.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `Occupation` class directly represents a profession or job, which perfectly matches the OIE type and all mentions.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

candidates.label: Credential
candidates.comment: A Credential is a certificate or document used to verify the identity, qualifications, or authority of a person or entity. Also called certificate, qualification, accreditation, license, identification. Examples: A driver's license, a university degree, a professional certification, a digital security certificate.

types.oie_definition: A division within a university or college that specializes in a particular academic discipline.
types.embedding_query_text: Academic Department: A division within a university or college that specializes in a particular academic discipline. Also called university department, faculty, school.

chosen_type.label: AcademicDepartment
chosen_type.definition: A division within a university or college that specializes in a particular academic discipline.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org class directly represents an academic department; `EducationalOrganization` is too broad, and other candidates are irrelevant.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: School
candidates.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

types.oie_definition: An institution providing medical and surgical treatment and nursing care for sick or injured people.
types.embedding_query_text: Hospital: An institution providing medical and surgical treatment and nursing care for sick or injured people. Also called medical center, clinic, healthcare facility.

chosen_type.label: Hospital
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `Hospital` class directly represents a medical institution providing patient treatment, which perfectly matches the OIE type and mention.

candidates.label: Hospital
candidates.comment: A Hospital is a civic structure and medical institution providing patient treatment with specialized medical and nursing staff and equipment. Also called medical center, clinic, healthcare facility. Examples: Mayo Clinic, Massachusetts General Hospital, a local emergency room.

candidates.label: MedicalClinic
candidates.comment: A medical business facility, often associated with a hospital, dedicated to specific diagnosis and/or healthcare, typically for outpatients but sometimes inpatients. Also called clinic, healthcare center, medical facility. Examples: a dermatology clinic, a walk-in clinic, a university health clinic, a family practice. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger institution providing comprehensive medical care.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: VeterinaryCare
candidates.comment: A local business or organization providing medical services for animals. Also called vet clinic, animal hospital, veterinary practice. Examples: a local veterinary office, an emergency animal hospital, a mobile vet service.

candidates.label: DiagnosticLab
candidates.comment: A medical organization that provides on-site or off-site diagnostic services, such as testing and analysis. Also called Medical laboratory, pathology lab, clinical lab, testing facility. Examples: Quest Diagnostics, LabCorp, a hospital's pathology department. Distinct from MedicalClinic, which provides direct patient care and consultations.

types.oie_definition: A rate, number, or amount in each hundred.
types.embedding_query_text: Percentage: A rate, number, or amount in each hundred. Also called proportion, rate, fraction.

chosen_type.label: Percentage
chosen_type.definition: A numerical value or proportion expressed as a fraction of 100.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org class specifically represents a percentage; `Quantity` and `Number` are too broad or focused on physical units.

candidates.label: HyperTocEntry
candidates.comment: A HyperTocEntry is a creative work representing an individual item or section within a HyperToc, specifying its associated media and time offsets. Also called table of contents item, media chapter, section marker. Examples: 'Introduction (0:00-5:30)', 'Keynote Speech (10:15-30:00)', 'Q&A Session (30:00-45:00)'.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Integer

candidates.label: ReturnLabelSourceEnumeration
candidates.comment: ReturnLabelSourceEnumeration is an Enumeration listing several types of return labels for product returns. Also called return shipping label source, label provision method. Examples: InStore, PrintAtHome, ProductReturnService, DownloadAndPrint.

candidates.label: MusicAlbumReleaseType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumReleaseType is an enumeration describing the kind of release for a music album. Also called release format, album release category. Examples: Single, EP, Album. Distinct from MusicAlbumProductionType, which describes the content type.

candidates.label: PurchaseType
candidates.comment: PurchaseType is an Enumeration listing different types of purchases for an item. Also called buying type, acquisition method. Examples: outright purchase, subscription, rental, lease.

candidates.label: RefundTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: RefundTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different kinds of product return refund types. Also called return refund category, reimbursement type. Examples: full refund, store credit, partial refund, exchange.

candidates.label: BedType
candidates.comment: A QualitativeValue enumeration representing a specific category or style of bed. Also called bed category, bed style, bed size. Examples: "King bed", "Queen bed", "Twin bed", "Sofa bed". Distinct from BedDetails, which describes the quantity and combination of beds.

types.oie_definition: A standard quantity used to express a physical quantity.
types.embedding_query_text: Unit of Measurement: A standard quantity used to express a physical quantity. Also called measure, metric, standard unit.

chosen_type.label: Mass
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `Mass` class explicitly includes "grams" as an example of a unit of measure for mass, which perfectly matches the OIE type and mention.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
candidates.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

types.oie_definition: A structured method for organizing and categorizing information or objects.
types.embedding_query_text: Classification System: A structured method for organizing and categorizing information or objects. Also called categorization system, taxonomy, typology.

chosen_type.label: CategoryCodeSet
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `CategoryCodeSet` class directly represents a classification system, explicitly listing "classification system" as an alias, which perfectly matches the OIE type and mention.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: CategoryCodeSet
candidates.comment: A creative work that defines a collection of related category codes. Also called classification system, code list, taxonomy. Examples: The UNSPSC classification, a company's internal product category list, a set of industry codes.

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

candidates.label: MedicineSystem
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing different systems of medical practice. Also called healthcare system, medical tradition, healing approach. Examples: "WesternConventional", "Ayurvedic", "TraditionalChineseMedicine", "Homeopathic".

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

types.oie_definition: A distinguishing quality or feature of something.
types.embedding_query_text: Characteristic: A distinguishing quality or feature of something. Also called attribute, feature, quality, trait.

chosen_type.label: PropertyValue
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `PropertyValue` class represents a feature or attribute value, explicitly listing "characteristic" as an alias, which perfectly matches the OIE type and mentions.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

types.oie_definition: A distinct division or group within a larger classification system.
types.embedding_query_text: Classification Category: A distinct division or group within a larger classification system. Also called category, class, grouping, segment.

chosen_type.label: CategoryCode
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `CategoryCode` class represents a specific code or term within a classification system, which aligns well with the concept of a "classification category" and the mentions.

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: CategoryCodeSet
candidates.comment: A creative work that defines a collection of related category codes. Also called classification system, code list, taxonomy. Examples: The UNSPSC classification, a company's internal product category list, a set of industry codes.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

candidates.label: SizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups used for various product categories. Also called size category, apparel size group, product size range. Examples: 'Adult', 'Kids', 'Petite', 'Plus Size'.

types.oie_definition: An individual animal, plant, or single-celled life form.
types.embedding_query_text: Organism: An individual animal, plant, or single-celled life form. Also called life form, living thing, biological entity.

chosen_type.label: Taxon
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `Taxon` class represents a cohesive biological unit or group of organisms, which perfectly matches the OIE type and mentions like "mold" and "bacteria".

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

types.oie_definition: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided.
types.embedding_query_text: Month: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided. Also called calendar month, period of weeks.

chosen_type.label: Month
chosen_type.definition: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org class directly represents a calendar month; existing candidates are irrelevant or too specific to media seasons.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Periodical
candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.oie_definition: A complex network of biologically functioning entities.
types.embedding_query_text: Biological System: A complex network of biologically functioning entities. Also called biological network, organ system, life system.

chosen_type.label: AnatomicalSystem
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `AnatomicalSystem` class represents a group of biological structures functioning together, which can encompass a complex biological system like "the gut microbiome".

candidates.label: AnatomicalSystem
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalSystem is a MedicalEntity comprising a group of anatomical structures that function together to perform a specific task. Also called organ system, biological system, body system. Examples: The circulatory system, the digestive system, the nervous system, the skeletal system. Distinct from AnatomicalStructure, which is an individual part of the body.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

candidates.label: Gene
candidates.comment: A Gene is a BioChemEntity representing a discrete unit of inheritance that affects one or more biological traits. Also called genetic unit, hereditary factor. Examples: FOXP2, SCARNA21, the gene for eye color, a specific allele.

candidates.label: MolecularEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical entity representing any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, or complex identifiable as a separate entity. Also called chemical entity, molecule, ion, compound. Examples: "water (H2O)", "glucose", "sodium ion (Na+)", "DNA". Distinct from BioChemEntity, which is a broader category for biological and chemical entities.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

types.oie_definition: A classification of a written or electronic record based on its content or purpose.
types.embedding_query_text: Document Type: A classification of a written or electronic record based on its content or purpose. Also called record type, file type, paper type.

chosen_type.label: DocumentType
chosen_type.definition: A classification of a written or electronic record based on its content or purpose.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org class directly represents a general document type; existing candidates are specific document instances or data types.

candidates.label: DigitalDocumentPermissionType
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific type of permission that can be granted for accessing a digital document. Also called Access level, permission role, document access type. Examples: ReadPermission, WritePermission, SharePermission, CommentPermission. Distinct from DigitalDocumentPermission, which is an instance of a permission granted to a specific entity.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: DataType
candidates.comment: DataType is a fundamental classification for the kind of values that can be stored or manipulated, such as numbers, text, or booleans. Also called primitive type, data format, value type. Examples: Integer, String, Boolean, Float, Date.

candidates.label: NoteDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A NoteDigitalDocument, as a DigitalDocument, is a file containing a note, primarily for the author's reference. Also called digital note, electronic memo, text note. Examples: a personal reminder in a digital format, a draft of an idea, a quick thought saved electronically. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is intended for public consumption.

types.oie_definition: The container or wrapping used to protect and present food products.
types.embedding_query_text: Food Packaging: The container or wrapping used to protect and present food products. Also called packaging, food container, wrapper.

chosen_type.label: FoodPackaging
chosen_type.definition: The container or wrapping used to protect and present food products.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org class directly represents food packaging; existing candidates are irrelevant.

candidates.label: FoodEvent
candidates.comment: A FoodEvent is an Event centered around food and drink. Also called culinary event, gastronomic event, food festival. Examples: A wine tasting, a cooking class, a food fair, a restaurant week promotion.

candidates.label: FoodService
candidates.comment: A FoodService is a Service related to providing food, such as breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Also called meal service, catering service, dining option. Examples: Breakfast service at a hotel, a school lunch program, an in-flight meal service, a catering package for an event.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: MenuItem
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a single food or drink item listed within a menu or menu section. Also called menu item, dish, beverage. Examples: "Spaghetti Carbonara", "Caesar Salad", "Coca-Cola", "Chocolate Lava Cake". Distinct from Menu, which is the entire list.

candidates.label: FoodEstablishmentReservation
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishmentReservation is a Reservation to dine at a food-related business. Also called restaurant booking, table reservation, dining reservation. Examples: A confirmed table booking at a restaurant, a reservation for a cafe, a booking for a private dining event. Distinct from Offer, which describes the availability of tables for booking.

types.oie_definition: A statement made on food packaging or advertising about the nutritional content or health benefits of a product.
types.embedding_query_text: Food Claim: A statement made on food packaging or advertising about the nutritional content or health benefits of a product. Also called nutritional claim, health claim, product assertion.

chosen_type.label: Claim
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org `Claim` class represents a specific, factually-oriented statement, which perfectly matches the OIE type and the mention "100% fruit".

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: ClaimReview
candidates.comment: A creative work that provides a fact-checking review of a specific claim. Also called fact-check, debunking, truth verification. Examples: A Snopes article debunking a viral claim, a PolitiFact rating of a politician's statement. Distinct from Review, which is a general assessment of an item.

candidates.label: NutritionInformation
candidates.comment: NutritionInformation, as a StructuredValue, provides details about the nutritional content of food, often for a recipe. Also called nutritional facts, food label information, dietary data. Examples: calorie count, fat content, protein amount, vitamin percentages. Distinct from Recipe, which describes how to prepare food.
